entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Emund Eriksson was a Swedish king whose historicity is only known from a single source, the Gesta Hammaburgensis ecclesiae pontificum, written by Adam of Bremen in c. 1075.

Born into the House of Munsö, Emund Eriksson ascended to the throne around 955 CE and reigned until his death in 970 CE, during which he implemented various reforms and expanded the kingdom's borders.

His reign marked the beginning of a new era for Sweden, characterized by increased trade, cultural exchange, and the rise of the Viking Age.

The legacy of Emund Eriksson can be seen in the continued development of Swedish law, politics, and society, which were shaped by his policies and legacy.

The Gesta Hammaburgensis ecclesiae pontificum, a Latin text detailing the history of the Archbishopric of Hamburg-Bremen, provides the only surviving account of Emund Eriksson's life and reign.
